title: Indefinite Articles
sourceNote: The auto-captions are garbled, and the exercise nouns in the video's mini-quiz could only partly be recovered; the exercises below are rebuilt from the rules taught in the video.
objectives: I can explain the difference between definite and indefinite articles
I can use ein and eine in the nominative
I know that there is no indefinite article in the plural
I can choose between ein/eine and der/die/das in a short text

grammar.title: Definite or indefinite?
grammar.body:
The **definite** article (*der, die, das*) points to one particular person or thing: *the* man. The **indefinite** article is used when we talk about any man, not a particular one: *a* man. English has *a / an* for this.

In a story you use the indefinite article first and the definite article when you speak about the same person again: *Das ist eine Frau. **Die** Frau ist schön.*

examples.de: Das ist eine Frau. Die Frau ist schön.
examples.en: That is a woman. The woman is beautiful.

grammar.title: The indefinite articles (nominative)
grammar.body:
The indefinite article depends on the gender, so you must know the definite article first:

- **der** → **ein**
- **die** → **eine**
- **das** → **ein** (same as masculine)

There is **no indefinite article in the plural**. You simply use the noun without an article.
grammar.ar: المفرد المذكّر والمحايد: ein، المؤنّث: eine، ولا يوجد أداة نكرة في الجمع.

grammar.title: Only the nominative
grammar.body: These forms are for the **nominative** case only. The other cases come in later lessons. You can only learn the indefinite article if you know the definite article of each noun.

mistakes.why: *Frau* is feminine (*die*), so the article is *eine*.
There is no indefinite article in the plural.
*Kind* is neuter (*das*), so the article is *ein*.

tip: Learn the definite article first: ein goes with der and das, eine goes with die.

comprehension.q: Which indefinite article goes with a masculine noun?
Which indefinite article goes with a feminine noun?

exercises.title: Ein or eine?
exercises.instructions: Write the indefinite article (ein or eine).

exercises.title: Indefinite or definite?
exercises.instructions: Choose the correct article for each gap. The first time we mention something we use the indefinite article.

items.q: Das ist ___ Mann. (ein / der) – ___ Mann ist alt. (ein / der)
Das ist ___ Frau. (eine / die) – ___ Frau ist schön. (eine / die)
Das ist ___ Kind. (ein / das) – ___ Kind ist glücklich. (ein / das)
Das ist ___ Blume. (eine / die) – ___ Blume ist schön. (eine / die)

items.expl: No indefinite article in the plural.

summary: Definite = a particular one (der, die, das); indefinite = any one (ein, eine).
der → ein, die → eine, das → ein.
There is no indefinite article in the plural.
First mention: ein/eine. Second mention: der/die/das.
These forms are for the nominative only.
